chunks: And from the hadith of Suwayd ibn Sa'id, who said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abul Khayr, from Abdullah ibn Amr
There is no doubt that it has been written in the Book of Allah: Twelve will rule over people.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the number of rulers or Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba* cites Abdullah ibn Amr to assert that the number twelve rulers is explicitly inscribed in the Quran, serving as a foundational proof for the Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams. While Sunni traditions often cite the hadith of 'twelve caliphs' from Bukhari and Muslim, this narration emphasizes a divine, Quranic predestination of their authority, distinguishing the Shia view of hereditary, infallible leadership from the elective nature of the caliphate.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (25) Suwayd bin Sa’eed narrated from Mu’tamir bin Sulayman from Hisham from ibn Seereen from Abul Khayr from Abdullah bin Amr: “
There is no doubt that it has been mentioned in the Book of Allah that twelve (caliphs) will rule over people.”
